facts.title: Code Isn't Memory: A Structural Codebase Index Inside a Coding Agent
facts.event_hint: Rigorous within-harness ablation showing a structural codebase index improves localization and resolve rate at lower cost per solve than agentic grep, with leak-audited per-task sandboxing.
facts.problem: Coding agents interleave LLMs with retrieval over the working repository, and retrieval implementations vary widely across deployed harnesses. It is unclear whether adding a structural codebase index to a coding agent actually changes cost or resolve rate when model and harness are held fixed.
facts.mechanism: Three experimental arms are compared inside a fixed coding-agent harness on a fixed model (Claude Opus 4.7), across three seeds, in a leak-audited per-task sandbox: (1) harness with the structural codebase index, (2) same harness without the index, (3) an agentic-grep comparator. A within-harness ablation isolates the index's effect; a cross-harness check verifies no regression against agentic grep. Per-cell exclusion ledger, leak-audit script, localization extractor, and results database are released.

evidence.claim: Within-harness ablation produces a large localization gain and a statistically separated resolve gain, with no cost penalty per cell and lower cost per solve.
Cross-harness check shows the index does not regress against an agentic-grep baseline on resolve or localization, again at no cost penalty.
Across seeds, the structural index lands at a lower $/solved than agentic grep.
Model held fixed as Claude Opus 4.7; benchmarks are SWE-PolyBench Verified and SWE-bench Pro; 3 seeds per condition.
evidence.condition: Claude Opus 4.7; 3 seeds; SWE-PolyBench Verified + SWE-bench Pro

evidence.claim: Index payoff is workload-dependent: structural ranking pays off when the workload includes multi-file changes.

facts.evaluation_context: Fixed harness + fixed model (Claude Opus 4.7); 3 seeds; benchmarks SWE-PolyBench Verified and SWE-bench Pro; leak-audited per-task sandbox; three arms (index / no-index / agentic-grep).
facts.limitations: Abstract reports directional/statistical results but no explicit numerical resolve-rate percentages or dollar figures; exact magnitudes require full text. Methodology soundness (leak audit) claimed but not independently verified here. Full body not fetched.
facts.project_relevance: Directly relevant to Agent acceleration / code-graph tooling: it provides controlled evidence that a structural codebase index (code-graph-style retrieval) improves both localization and resolve rate while lowering cost-per-solve, and identifies multi-file changes as the workload where structural ranking pays off. This validates investment in code-graph indexes for coding agents.
